issue_context.title: [API Proposal]:  make SocketAddress more useful
comments: AFAIR SocketAddress does not store a port, you need to use an IPEndPoint for that?

@wfurt the usage example only demonstrates the part of the proposed API that is intended to be consumed by end users. It would be more interesting to see how socket code implementing #87397 will interact with the new methods. Can you share your POC for that?

Some specific questions:
- Do we really need a setter for `SocketBuffer`?
- Would growing `Size` extend the buffer implicitly, and as a result invalidate all the `Memory<byte>` references to the previous buffer, or shall we better disallow such a case?

The setter for `SocketBuffer` is not needed for the internal socket refactor. My PoC moved everything from array to memory<byte> and uses `Pin` method when needed to. I envisioned somebody passing pre-pinned memory so we would save allocation for GCHandle/MemoryHandle for each operation for async processing. That goes above and beyond the original asks but it would help IMHO with memory management in certain cases. 

And I don't plan to allow buffer growing. Attempt to grow size beyond buffer size would throw. We really only need to string it down in certain cases - like UDS.

> envisioned somebody passing pre-pinned memory so we would save allocation for GCHandle/MemoryHandle for each operation for async processing. 

Considering that we disallow growing the buffer, wouldn't it be then better to pass the `Memory<byte>` in a constructor in this use-case?

we could. I feel that the setter is more flexible but that is also something API review may care about. (there is already internal constructor that takes Span<byte> but that allocates the array internally and it it does data copy) 

On the other hand, this is not critical for any work I plan for 8.0 so we can also take it out for now and do it later as needed.

review_comments: This test fully covers everything added? Presumably we need tests for the new SocketAddress surface area?
I will add more tests for SocketAddress. While this should cover the main use I think I can add some more test for invalid cases.
I added more tests to cover more including short SocketAddress passed in and new SocketAddress API.
Do we need to slice socketAddress.Buffer to socketAddress.Size?

That is done by the SocketAddress e.g. it returns internal buffer up to the Size. (e.g. it does not show whole underlying buffer). Without it, it would be hard to use IMHO as everybody would need to keep slicing.

According to this line, it's sliced to InternalSize, not Size:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/88970/files#diff-840f5a24cac9941cc101bdffdd4772c982b00fe9b71e2aa8aa48a95746d4fa96R161
Can't those be different?  And in the API review, I thought we'd said that was correct, that Buffer would always return the full buffer (such a developer would know the maximum value it could be), and then they could slice down to Size if Size might be smaller.  Are you suggesting we should diverge from that?

Perhaps I misunderstood the question during review. Size can be sliced down to be less than buffer size but effectively it is `InternalSize`. (e.g. InternalSize holds the visible/valid part of the InternalBuffer)

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/8f70860b23845e7b6a2fc31c1edf699d3ee2935d/src/libraries/Common/src/System/Net/SocketAddress.cs#L47-L53

When SocketAddress is created for given `AddressFamily`  `Size`/`InternalSize` is set to appropriate length and the buffer length is exactly that (as we do not Rent from pool) Somebody can check that or use the new `GetMaximumAddressSize`

We can make it to return always the full buffer if you feel it is better. It may be more work to get the correct data (e.g. Slicing) and Im not sure if there is value getting access to parts that do not hold valid content. 
This really matters only for Receiving, right?

> InternalSize holds the visible/valid part of the InternalBuffer

Ok. It's confusing that we have both Size and InternalSize, when they're actually the same thing (I thought they were different).  We should rename `InternalSize` to be `_size`.

> We can make it to return always the full buffer if you feel it is better. It may be more work to get the correct data (e.g. Slicing) and Im not sure if there is value getting access to parts that do not hold valid content.
This really matters only for Receiving, right?

I don't have a super strong opinion.  If you feel that what you have is better and will lead to more folks falling into the pit of success, I'm ok with it.  We should then be clear in the documentation that Buffer.Length always equals Size but the internal buffer may actually be larger, and if you want to set Size, you can set it up to the value it originally was when the SocketAddress was constructed.
agreed. I'll make the naming change Ince I weed out all the direct internal access e.g.  `InternalSize` and `InternalBuffer` become private.

I decided to keep the Buffer sliced to current address to make it easier to use. The only one case IMHO where this may be tricky is SocketAddress constructive when somebody would explicit put smaller size than needed. I added test and it would fail with strange address error on Windows and it did hit some assets in Socket PAL on Linux. So I added chart to make sure passed SA is always good enough. This should always be the case for internal use in Sockets. I will rename InternalSize in follow-up PR.
Same question for all of these....
Do we need both?  Should we just always use the one that uses ints and cast to int from AddressFamily/SocketType/ProtocolType when we have them?
updated + cast in SocketPal
Do any of the supplied callback delegates actually use anything from the socket address other than its length?
no. for sending we really do not need anything other than set the transferred bytes. However the core part is shared between send and receive so I decided to keep it.
Is this just an automated change from the genapi tool?
yes, it is. I was thinking that it would be nice to update ref assemblies always on tool updates so this is weeded out. Or I can cherry pick just the relevant changes.
You're going to rename these both subsequently, right?
yes.
Should we assert that the address family is either IPv6 or IPv4?
Is this a bug fix?

I'm not sure but possibly yes. On Windows we seems to get the address but it fails on Linux. Perhaps we can also check if this is TCP and get the value from `RemoteEndPoint`? I can write issue for improvement and investigation. 
I had trouble because setting `Size` zero would throw. Alternatively we can allow it to indicate that the buffer does not have any valid address.
Same question as earlier for these... we don't need to splice it down to Size?
